units: Y. Hor. I, 46ᵃ bot. (ref. to Num. XV, 24, העדה) כל השבטים קרויין ק׳ all tribes together are called ḳahal; כל שבט … ק׳ every tribe for itself is called ḳ.; Bab.
<cite ref="Horayot 3a:20">Hor. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>כגון … רובו של ק׳ וכ׳</he> when six tribes have sinned, and they form the majority of the congregation (the entire people) &c.
Ib. הני הוא דאיקרו ק׳ only they (the entire people) are called ḳ.—

<cite ref="Kiddushin 73a:2">Kidd. 73ᵃ</cite> <he>קְהַל ודאי</he> a community of Israelites of undoubted legitimacy; <he>קְ׳ ספק</he> of doubtful legitimacy; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 8:2:6">Y. Yeb. VIII, 9ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>קָ׳ ברור</he>; <he>קְ׳ ספק</he>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 8:2:6">Ib.</cite> [read:] <he>ארבע קְהִילּוֹת אינון קְ׳ יי׳ קְ׳ כהנים וכ׳</he> four communities are meant by ‘the congregation of the Lord’ (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 23:2">Deut. XXIII, 2</cite>; <cite ref="Deuteronomy 23:3">3</cite>; <cite ref="Deuteronomy 23:4">4</cite>; <cite ref="Deuteronomy 23:9">9</cite>): the community of priests, of Levites, of Israelites, and of proselytes. Mish. ib. VIII, 2 <he>ואינן … אלא מלבא בק׳</he> and they are forbidden only to enter the congregation (to intermarry with Israelites); a. fr.—Pl., v. <cite ref="S00211"><he>קְהִלָּה</he></cite>
